name: Bear
notes: Billed from Redford, Michigan; lost a first-round National Title tournament match to Havok on Wednesday Night WarZone (22 April 1998) after briefly turning the bout around with a reverse DDT off a lifted Gorilla Slam attempt.
caption: Turned a lifted Gorilla Slam into a reverse DDT, but still lost his National Title tournament opener to Havok.

identity.note: A stock ring name; nothing but the word ties this record to the existing Summit entity, which itself is already recorded distinct from every other same-named entity in the registry. No roster or operator overlap found.

name: Havok
notes: Billed from Los Angeles, California, wrestling expressionless throughout; won a first-round National Title tournament match over Bear with a top-rope double axe-handle, a chair shot, and his own finisher, the Havok-Bomb (a jackknife powerbomb), in 27 minutes 16 seconds on Wednesday Night WarZone (22 April 1998).
caption: Won his National Title tournament opener over Bear with a chair shot and his own Havok-Bomb finisher.

name: Cobra

name: Guru

name: Dentist DDS
notes: Billed from parts unknown, "earning his revenge after the loss of his license" and accompanied by manager Hygenist; won a first-round National Title tournament match over Guru by countout, aided by his manager's distraction of the referee and an unseen pair of brass knuckles, on Wednesday Night WarZone (22 April 1998).

name: "Sensational" Christian Hardcastle

tenures.note: Forms a "demented alliance" with Mister Meanor against "Heartbreaker" Steve Wallace at Spring Fest 98 (31 May 1998), losing a two-on-one handicap match; a backstage vignette at Boston Massacre (27 June 1998) reveals his own alter ego, "Da Yellow Guy," without further explanation in the held record.

notes: Billed from Alberta, Canada; won a first-round World Heavyweight Title tournament match over Jack Vars with a top-rope splash (the "490 splash") on Wednesday Night WarZone (22 April 1998), after Vars's own valet, Cindy, was accidentally kissed unconscious mid-match and then tripped Vars during a late comeback attempt. Formed a "demented alliance" with Mister Meanor a month later, losing a two-on-one handicap match to Steve Wallace at Spring Fest 98.
caption: Won a back-and-forth World Title tournament opener over Jack Vars, then formed a "demented alliance" with Mister Meanor that came up short two-on-one against Steve Wallace.

name: Jack Vars

tenures.note: Loses a singles match to "Brutal" Brian Floyd at the promotion's own final surviving broadcast, without his valet Cindy appearing again in the held record.

tenures.source: Billed from Truth or Consequences, New Mexico with valet Cindy McGlothlan -- matching this record's own existing tenure -- as "the man that has held over 50 titles," Jack Vars loses the founding tournament's main event to CandyMan, then wins a non-tournament match over James Miller, on Monday Night Elite (12 and 19 October 1998); billed for the promotion's own first supercard, defending -- as challenger -- against CandyMan for the World Heavyweight Championship on 29 November 1998, a date the held record does not reach.

notes: Billed from Truth or Consequences, New Mexico, accompanied by valet Cindy; lost a first-round World Heavyweight Title tournament match to "Sensational" Christian Hardcastle on Wednesday Night WarZone (22 April 1998) after Cindy was accidentally kissed unconscious by Hardcastle mid-match and later tripped Vars during his own comeback attempt. Lost again to "Brutal" Brian Floyd at the promotion's own final surviving broadcast.
caption: Lost a back-and-forth World Title tournament opener to Christian Hardcastle after his own valet accidentally cost him the finish, then lost again to "Brutal" Brian Floyd two months later.

name: Aries "The God of War"

tenures.note: Wins two further World Heavyweight Title Tournament rounds (Saturday Night Showcase, 25 April, and a match not otherwise detailed in the held record) to reach the tournament final at Spring Fest 98 (31 May 1998), where he loses the title match to Ian Walsh; fights in the winning War Games team at Boston Massacre (27 June) and loses a title-eliminator match to Creed at the promotion's own final surviving broadcast after Doomsday's own unexplained interference.

notes: Introduced in a post-match interview segment on Wednesday Night WarZone (22 April 1998), promising to become "the feared man" in the promotion and naming a first opponent (unminted, not otherwise attested); won his way to the main event of Spring Fest 98 (31 May 1998), losing a near-hour-long tournament final to Ian Walsh for the vacant World Heavyweight Championship.
caption: Cut a menacing debut promo naming himself the future of the promotion's title picture, then fell just short of it in a near-hour-long tournament final against Ian Walsh.
